claims.text: Integrating machine-learning models with first-principles calculations can improve determination of the solid-to-fluid transition temperature in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
The integrated approach can improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy.
The integrated approach can improve determination of volume change at the transition.
The integrated approach can improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
PSSOS is an example of integrating machine learning with first-principles calculations.
Machine-learning models can facilitate screening of large compositional spaces in multicomponent or high-entropy materials.
Machine-learning models can identify patterns in thermodynamic properties relevant to the high-temperature solid-to-fluid transition.
First-principles calculations accurately predict transition temperatures and the other listed transition properties.
The intervention will improve predictive accuracy relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve computational efficiency relative to existing methods such as DFT free-energy studies and TOR-TILD.
PSSOS provides comparable accuracy to SQS while significantly improving efficiency for high-entropy-alloy screening.
The proposed intervention is limited to high-temperature, multicomponent systems.
The accuracy of the machine-learning component may depend on training-data quality.
The first-principles component may remain computationally expensive.
Comparison with experimental measurements across a set of multicomponent high-entropy materials can test the predicted transition properties.
